messages:
samir: quick check — for the SDK, are we leaning towards a single 'stream' primitive that covers both paged and streaming responses, or keep separate Paginator vs Stream APIs?

elaine: i prefer separate. stream implies server push, cursors are pull-y. mixing hurts ergonomics across go/py/ts.

samir: main push is DRY — one iterable that yields either items or chunks, auto-resumes on retries. but worried about language mismatch (goroutines vs async iter).

tori: +1 on separate. Go wants channel-ish semantics, TS has async iter, python has both sync and async — surface diverges.

ben-ops: also ops concern: transport choice affects resume semantics. with HTTP/1.1 streaming we can't reliably resume mid-stream. grpc+http2 gives stronger stream ids and easier resume.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary rolled to eng-staging at 11:02 — note: streaming endpoint currently uses h2c behind envoy.

elaine: for retries: we should attach an opaque continuation token for paged endpoints. For true streaming, require idempotent resume tokens in proto header and a monotonic `sequence_id` per event.

samir: draft API proposal idea:

```
// TS
const it = client.listWidgets({pageSize: 100}) // returns AsyncIterable<Widget>
for await (const w of it) { /*...*/ }

// Stream (server push)
const s = client.streamEvents(); // returns EventStream with .on('data') and .resume(token)
```

elaine: docs concern: users expect `for await` to just work. we need backpressure handling and cancellation signals (abort controller or context).

tori: backoff strategy: exponential with jitter, but on resume we need to be careful about duplicate items. include `sequence_id` per item when possible and surface de-dup hints.

ben-ops: metadata idea: use `x-redwood-continue` header for continuation tokens, and `x-redwood-seq` per message. make tokens opaque JWT-like so we can encode shard/offset.

samir: OK action items: 1) samir + elaine to sketch TS/PY/GO surface variants (sync vs async semantics) ; 2) infra to prototype resume header on grpc stream and an envoy filter that preserves h2 stream ids; 3) tori to run a small eval to measure duplicate rate with tokens vs sequence id dedupe.

elaine: i'll draft a short compatibility table and post a follow-up RFC link with examples for sync/async languages. will highlight which transports support resume natively.

tori: if we do separate surfaces, we should still provide a small adapter in each SDK that converts stream->paged (and vice versa) where safe. lowers user friction.

ben-ops: note on security: continuation tokens must be scoped to the customer and short-lived for shared endpoints. for private deployments we can relax lifetime.

samir: cool — i'll collect sketches and turn into a one-pager. ping here if you want to join the RFC review. :thumbsup:
